repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
    wait until((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == false)
    triggered = false
}
wait until((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == true)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(100, 0)
delay(3 SEC)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(0, 0)
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR specifies a rising-edge wait followed by actions. The candidate polls the sensor at the start of the cycle (t=0) and finds it false, so the guard fails and no action occurs. At t=100ms, the motion becomes true, but the candidate has already passed the guard check and will not re-evaluate until the next cycle start (t=1000ms), missing the required action at 100ms. This is the 'repeating rising edge implemented as periodic polling' mismatch (Example A).
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic polling `if` with a blocking rising-edge wait pattern. The script now blocks until motion becomes true (handling the initial false state correctly), executes the body immediately upon transition, and then re-arms by waiting for the false state before the next cycle can fire.
